chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Minqari, from Yunus or al-Mufaddal, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
There is no Friday night except that in it there is joy for the awliya' of Allah.
I said: How is that, may I be your ransom?

He عليه السلام said: When it is Friday night, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله comes to the Throne, and the Imams عليهم السلام come, and I come with them. Then I do not return except with acquired knowledge, and were it not for that, what is with me would be exhausted.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ اللَّهِ: the awliya' of Allah, those granted closeness to Him
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: the Imams, the divinely appointed leaders
key_terms.الْعَرْشَ: the Throne, the exalted station mentioned in the narration
key_terms.بِعِلْمٍ مُسْتَفَادٍ: with acquired knowledge, meaning knowledge newly received
key_terms.سُرُورٌ: joy or gladness occurring on that night
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ جُمُعَةٍ: the night of Friday, described here as a special time

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the increase of the Imams' knowledge on Friday night?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a special distinction of Friday night for the awliya' of Allah and particularly for the Imam عليه السلام. It states that on Friday night the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and the Imams عليهم السلام attend the Throne, and the Imam returns with renewed, acquired knowledge. The narration highlights the ongoing divine bestowal of knowledge upon the Imams عليهم السلام.
